correctness.rationale: Every quadrilateral is affinely diagonal-normalized, with all parameter boundaries stated. Four exact facet normals yield necessary/sufficient translated containment inequalities. Three explicit nonnegative coefficients cancel normals and force a lower bound. A solved candidate center meets that bound with a nonnegative fourth-facet slack, including the separate singular parallelogram case. Triangle chord lengths are a tent function; after a coordinate reversal its lambda-Steiner image is precisely the same normalized quadrilateral. Strict branch monotonicity and explicit directions prove the exact sharp range. Independent rational calculations checked 11,724 pairs but are not used as infinite proof.

evidence: Bakaev--Yehudayoff prove a general affine-invariant characterization and stability near simplices; they give no formula specifying the quadrilateral parameter dependence in the inspected portions.

Kobos--Varivoda, On the Banach--Mazur Distance in Small Dimensions (2024), establishes classical planar bounds 1<=s<=2, uniqueness of planar critical centers, and triangle/symmetric equality; no exact two-parameter formula was identified from accessible material.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The fact that every planar convex body has asymmetry between 1 and 2 does not imply the exact diagonal expression or the sharp minimum for each generalized Steiner parameter. Nor does a stability theorem near triangles determine all intermediate diagonal fractions. Full coverage in older books remains possible and has not been ruled out by the inspected material.

originality.rationale: A complete intrinsic two-diagonal formula for the classical Minkowski containment asymmetry of every planar convex quadrilateral, and its sharp one-step triangular lambda-Steiner profile, were not obtained from the closest published primary sources or accessible mathematical-record searches. The closest results use different invariants (centroid-chord ratio), domains (parallel-opposite hexagons), or qualitative random convergence/central symmetry. A latent equivalent older formula remains a real historical-priority risk; search absence is not an originality proof.

value.rationale: The quantities are intrinsic and motivated: classical Minkowski containment asymmetry on the full two-dimensional affine moduli of quadrilaterals, and a sharp quantitative one-step geometric invariant for a recent interpolation between shaking and Steiner symmetrization. Both the complete formula and a two-branch directional optimizer classification cover all proper parameter choices. They are structural facts for a natural class, rather than a random numerical case; the expected use is as a benchmark for non-iterative shape control and for detecting when an intermediate operation creates a nearly central-symmetric figure. Limits to triangles/quadrilaterals are explicit.
